articles.title: IBM quantum computer solves problem classical computers can’t in just 15 minutes
articles.summary: IBM and University of Chicago researchers have demonstrated that a quantum computer can complete an extraordinarily complex calculation in just 15 minutes, beyond the practical reach of leading classical computing methods. A novel error-detection technique also allows scientists to establish confidence in the accuracy of the results, overcoming a major hurdle in quantum computing.

articles.summary: Last year, Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that's designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows about its users. articles.title: Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
articles.summary: Scientists have developed a new way to determine whether quantum simulations can be trusted, solving a growing problem as quantum computers become too powerful for conventional machines to check. Demonstrated on a 51-qubit system, the technique measures uncertainty and provides verifiable error margins that could help unlock the full potential of quantum computing.

articles.title: Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a faster way to identify diamond-based materials that could power quantum computers and sensors at room temperature. The breakthrough has already revealed promising new quantum building blocks that could help unlock computing capabilities far beyond those of today's supercomputers.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI proves why efficiency isn’t a virtue
articles.summary: On the same day that Anthropic entered the public market, a painstakingly human video game became one of most successful entertainment launches of all time.

articles.title: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York
articles.summary: New York has banned AI chatbot toys for five years as new research from Common Sense Media reveals troubling safety failures, including exposure to inappropriate content and risks to emotional development.

articles.title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
articles.summary: The proposed Character.ai bankruptcy sale includes sensitive personal data from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, including 2.1 million registered to minors, the state AGs said.

articles.title: AI data centers are becoming harder to build, and neoclouds are feeling it
articles.summary: ⁠Nvidia has made clear⁠ it won’t backstop an AI data center until it’s nearly ready to run, and that’s landing just as neoclouds report construction delays and more expensive debt. The message to developers is that land, power, and a finished building matter more than a pitch deck.  ⁠Anita Verma-Lallian⁠ has been selling exactly that. […]

articles.title: Building critical hardware for Canada's first quantum satellite mission
articles.summary: The Institute for Quantum Computing (IQC) team selected by the Canadian Space Agency to lead the science of the Quantum Encryption and Science Satellite (QEYSSat)—Canada's first quantum satellite mission—has recently delivered two quantum sources to the Canadian Space Agency (CSA) that will transmit encrypted signals from Earth to the satellite. This marks a major milestone for the QEYSSat project, and IQC students have played a crucial role.

articles.title: Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun

articles.title: 42 state AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from selling users’ chats
articles.summary: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to prevent Character.AI from selling off user data as it navigates Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. In a deluge of nearly identical press releases, the various AGs accuse the company of planning to auction off "the private chat histories of more than 21 million U.S. accounts - […]

articles.title: FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
articles.summary: In an announcement on Wednesday, the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company's "Starmind" initiative. With several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space, including Google and Blue Origin, this is the first approval the agency […]

articles.title: Nothing offers a full look at its AI earbuds and charging case
articles.summary: Nothing is showing off a much more detailed look at its upcoming AI earbuds ahead of their December 8th release. The Ear Note buds can record your calls, while their charging case can record, transcribe, and summarize your conversations. Like the Ear 3, the Ear Note's microphone-equipped case comes with a "Talk" button that you […]

articles.title: Amazon is reportedly in talks to end Muse AI shopping block
articles.summary: Amazon has held talks about letting Meta's Muse AI agent shop on its online marketplace, according to a report from Fortune. The discussions, which could end Amazon's block on Muse, reportedly center on the kinds of products the AI agent recommends and the potential impact on the ecommerce giant's advertising revenue. As reported by Fortune, […]

articles.title: Has vibe coding made open source the new normal for synths?
articles.summary: The emergence of powerful vibe-coding agents and tools like Reverse Engineer Anything has caused chaos in the music gear world, leaving companies scrambling to figure out how to respond. While some, like Roland, have remained silent for now, others have embraced the modding community. In the last several weeks, as it's become clear that no […]

articles.title: David Fincher is being dragged for suspected use of AI in his latest film
articles.summary: Though David Fincher's fans had been eagerly anticipating The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, early screenings of the Once Upon a Time in Hollywood sequel starring Brad Pitt have raised questions about whether generative AI was used in the film. People have claimed that the movie is chock-full of uncanny, inconsistent visuals that make it […]

articles.title: Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
articles.summary: Tidal is officially banning AI-generated music on December 9th. As a result of this change, Tidal will delete around 29 million AI-generated songs and reject an estimated 80,000 to 85,000 tracks per day, according to Tidal music lead Robert Andersen. The move comes just months after Tidal began labeling and demonetizing tracks identified as 100 […]

articles.title: What is a thought made of? Why human consciousness may be beyond AI’s reach
articles.summary: A new theory suggests that the brain may chemically encode and retrieve memories rather than relying solely on electrical signals. Researchers propose that interactions between brain cells and their molecular surroundings could help explain the intimate connection between memory, emotion, and thought. Their findings challenge the assumption that increasingly powerful computers could eventually develop human-like consciousness.

articles.title: Strange new materials can crawl, walk, and dig like living creatures
articles.summary: Scientists have developed remarkable materials that can crawl, walk, and dig using their own internal energy, potentially paving the way for a new generation of autonomous soft robots. They also discovered that making individual components more active can paradoxically make the entire material less responsive, challenging a long-standing principle of engineering.

articles.title: AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover
articles.summary: AI may not think like the human brain after all, according to a striking new discovery that challenges how scientists understand artificial intelligence. Researchers found that even AI models that closely predict brain activity may rely on internal processes the brain doesn't use, raising important questions about their reliability in neuroscience research.

articles.title: AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
articles.summary: Scientists have developed an AI tool that can uncover hidden warning signs of bladder cancer up to five years before diagnosis, identifying 85% of cases in a major study involving nearly 70,000 patients. By revealing subtle patterns that conventional screening misses, the technology could help doctors detect cancer earlier and spare patients unnecessary invasive procedures.

articles.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
articles.summary: A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful. Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them.

articles.title: AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden warning sign in routine heart scans that could predict sudden cardiac death before it strikes. The AI-powered discovery outperformed conventional screening methods, potentially revealing thousands of people at risk of a fatal heart malfunction that doctors might otherwise miss.

articles.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
articles.summary: Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.

articles.title: 76% of Australians are struggling to tell apart real and AI content
articles.summary: Most Australians are using—or at least have tried out—generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT, Copilot and Gemini, among many others.

articles.title: We built an AI you can dance with. It taught us about developing the technology responsibly
articles.summary: In recent months, top researchers have quit leading artificial intelligence companies, warning the AI race is moving too quickly, with too little oversight and accountability.

articles.title: Climate change could expose underwater internet cables to fishing damage
articles.summary: From online banking and video calls to international communications, everyday life relies on a vast network of cables hidden beneath the sea. But climate change could create new threats to the underwater cables that keep the world connected, according to new research involving scientists at the National Oceanography Center (NOC).

articles.title: Q&A: Evolutionary algorithms may automate the search for better energy forecasting model settings
articles.summary: A doctoral dissertation of Aleksei Vakhnin in the field of Environmental Science will be examined at the Faculty of Science, Forestry and Technology, Kuopio campus.

articles.title: Free will is not an illusion but a control achievement of the brain—and it can be tested in machines
articles.summary: Is free will real, or is it an illusion created by our brains? For neuroscientist Paul Verschure, distinguished university professor at Miguel Hernández University of Elche (UMH), in Spain, free will is real—and measurable. In two papers published in Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B, he argues that free will is a product of evolution and introduces the concept of Responsible Autonomy: six control capacities that allow an agent, human or otherwise, to govern its own behavior.

articles.title: A gadget straight out of a James Bond film: Tiny tooth-mounted sensor recognizes silent speech
articles.summary: Speaking unobtrusively with artificial intelligence may one day be possible with a small sensor attached to a tooth. The sensor recognizes the wearer's words as they mouth them naturally and silently, remaining completely hidden from outside view.

articles.title: Solar-powered system targets fouling in complex wastewater treatment
articles.summary: Researchers at the Xinjiang Technical Institute of Physics and Chemistry (XTIPC) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) have developed a solar-powered electrocoagulation–membrane filtration (SPEC-MF) system to reduce membrane fouling during the treatment of oily and complex organic wastewater.

articles.title: Salty lake water helps a zinc battery keep working at −50°C
articles.summary: Extreme cold can affect a water-based battery's ability to deliver electricity. Its liquid electrolyte—the fluid that carries charge—can freeze, while the charged particles moving through it slow down. Researchers have now built a rechargeable zinc battery that works at −50°C (−58°F) using saline lake water as a starting ingredient.

articles.title: It's making your list, and checking your price: Holiday shopping goes AI
articles.summary: From sales that seem to start earlier each year to a dwindling desire by shoppers to camp outside of big-box stores in the early morning to snag the best deals, Black Friday has changed over the years.
